author: barnabasbusa
content:
going further, sometime next year I'd like to propose to further increase the minimum bar for a PFI. maybe for I* we can already do this. 

A minimum requirement of a single client prototype implementation should be the minimum requirement for a PFI eligibility.

author: barnabasbusa
content: I think its important to keep the process up to date with the available tools we got at hand, and we shouldn't try to artificially limit ourselves just to bow for "traditions"

author: spencer_tb
content:
Generally I like this as it moves us much further ahead before CFI-ing. I'll always be in favour of these initiatives. I personally want a PQ safe Ethereum ASAP. 

One concern I can think of, which I've heard from others before, is that it may be too much of a hurdle for non technical people to propose an EIP that could benefit Ethereum. On the other side, in an age of AI this hurdle is reduced.

On the EL, currently we have EIPs "SHOULD" have a specs/tests implementation in EELS before CFI. Moving the "SHOULD" to a "MUST" could be a better step in the CFI process over changing the PFI process.

I think `@lightclient` commented yesterday that specs/tests (alone)  have less value now with AI, which I tend to agree with. For me now, specs/tests with 2 (or X) client implementations should be the new bar somewhat for CFI. The key here is to move from underspecification to fully specified earlier in the process, which multiple implementations unlock.

author: trent_vanepps
content:
digging.. 🪏 

Under PR #2275, 22 of the 68 Hegota EIPs would have been kept off ACD calls at the point they were actually discussed, because each was still an open PR in ethereum/EIPs. Together they used about 250 minutes (roughly 4.2 hours) of call time before being merged.

8 of those EIPs (8184, 8334, 8341, 8358, 8359, 8367, 8374, 8375) were never merged before their decision. They took about 70 minutes across 8 ACD calls, which is the call time the rule would actually have saved. Seven of them were declined (DFI), and 8334 is still PFI.

The other 14 were merged a median of 14 days after their first call (average about 15, range 0 to 34 days). They took about 180 minutes, which the rule would have pushed to later calls rather than removed. 8363 (Tapered Issuance Burn) was the largest single item: 32 minutes on ACDC 184, five days before it merged.
